claim_to_test: A learner can distinguish how two legal moves change one specific immediate opponent reply in an unseen position, and explain the relevant capture-line change.
task: Choose one legal root move that denies the stated reply and another legal root move that permits it. Record the first pair and written reason before revealing feedback.
feedback: Replay both root moves, show a legal capture ray on the allowing board and changed cells on that ray. Verify every immediate reply in both boards. Also show a newly opened reply when the blocking move creates one.

reason_rubric_for_human_review.0: No relevant difference, or a claim contradicting the board or rules.
reason_rubric_for_human_review.1: Names a relevant changed square or reply but does not explain how the two choices affect the capture.
reason_rubric_for_human_review.2: Correctly relates the changed square, opposing capture ray and legal status of the target reply under both choices, without claiming this proves strongest play.

selection: First qualifying distinct position per fixed completed native Edax game, plies 12–44. Require at least three legal root moves, both denying and allowing choices, and a target that is not itself a root legal move or corner. Exclude positions in the current game including rotations, reflections and color swaps; exclude previously answered exercises in the session.
scope: The goal concerns a specified immediate opportunity. Denying one reply may open others and does not prove that the blocking move has a higher search score, is strongest, or wins.
formal_evaluation: Use the independent-game separation, blinded reason grading, baseline and recommendation-only comparison specified by decision-teaching-v1. The shipped public practice bank is not a sealed assessment set. No expert review or learner benefit has been established.
